t: Except for benefits provided under section 7 of this Act, nothing in this or any other Act of Congress shall be construed to make the increases authorized herein applicable to military personnel or to any person or employees not within the definition of “employee” in section 40(b)(1) or (2) of the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act. However, these amendments shall apply to employees of the government of the District of Columbia other than members of the Police and Fire Departments who are pensioned or pensionable under the provisions of the Policemen’s and Firemen’s Retirement and Disability Act.

fable.w: This section only defines which employees the compensation increases cover: it excludes military personnel and includes certain District of Columbia employees. The tempting reading is that the mention of District of Columbia government employees brings in a non-federal party, but they appear only as recipients of benefits, not as parties consulted on a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.
fable.s: nothing in this or any other Act of Congress shall be construed to make the increases authorized herein applicable to military personnel

qwen_block.w: This section defines the scope of applicability for certain benefit increases, specifying which groups of federal employees and military personnel are included or excluded. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or non-federal entities) before a decision is made. The text is purely definitional and administrative regarding internal government benefits.
qwen_block.s: Except for benefits provided under section 7 of this Act, nothing in this or any other Act of Congress shall be construed to make the increases authorized herein applicable to military personnel or to any person or employees not within the definition of “employee” in section 40(b)(1) or (2) of the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act.

opus.w: This section only sets who the benefit increases under the Federal Employees' Compensation Act cover. It leaves out military personnel and includes District of Columbia employees, except police and fire department members. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. Naming D.C. employees as people the benefits apply to does not bring them into any federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting wrong reading is to treat the mention of District of Columbia government employees as an outside, non-federal party being involved. That fails because the section only says who the compensation increases apply to. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the eligibility criteria for certain pay increases or benefits. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in the decision-making process of the federal government. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants from the scope of participation. Therefore, despite affecting non-federal employees (like D.C. workers), the text describes the application of a statutory rule rather than a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Except for benefits provided under section 7 of this Act, nothing in this or any other Act of Congress shall be construed to make the increases authorized herein applicable to military personnel or to any person or employees not within the definition of “employee” in section 40(b)(1) or (2) of the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining who is eligible for benefits involves "participation" because it affects people outside the government (like D.C. employees). However, the definition explicitly states that participation "does not include applications for benefits or grants." This section merely defines the scope of eligibility for a pay increase/benefit; it does not establish a process for outsiders to consult with the government, comment on a decision, or serve on an advisory body. The actors involved in the decision-making (Congress, the Secretary, etc.) are all inside the federal government, and the text describes the application of a rule, not a participatory process.
